column1: #zone label(martial_quarter) start(1; 1) message(A martial quarter of three separate zones
column2: each painted from one anchor cell: an archery range
column4: and a tomb. shoot_from=south stands archers at the south end firing north at targets you build there. Apply with the cursor on the top-left tile; every (WxH) extent fills down and to the right from its anchor.)

column1: tags: zone, archery range, barracks, tomb, military, directional

description: The corpus's first DIRECTIONAL zone property and three untried zone types in one martial-themed blueprint. An archery range a takes shoot_from (west/left/east/right/north/top/south/bottom
column2: default west): it points the range so archers stand at that end and fire toward the opposite wall. Here shoot_from=south makes a 3-wide
column3: 8-tall shooting lane where dwarves loose arrows northward. That is a zone-level direction
column4: unlike the directional #build tokens the corpus already shows (the drawbridge gw and the screw pump Msu point a building
column5: not a zone). A barracks B beside it is the muster and training ground for the squad. A tomb T carries its own two properties: pets=true lets war animals be interred alongside their owner
column6: and citizens=false reserves the crypt so ordinary citizens are not buried here (drop citizens=false and any dwarf may claim it). Each zone is one anchor cell with a (WxH) extent that fills down and to the right
column7: so the three rectangles never overlap. What the blueprint cannot place for you: the archery range needs archery targets
column9: built at the far north end so archers shoot into them
column10: and a tomb is only useful once a coffin is built inside it and assigned to a soldier. Paint the zones first
column11: then lay a #build blueprint over the same tiles for the targets and coffins.
